title: Competency questions
examples: How do I know when I should take the lead in a group?
What is the difference between leading and managing a team?
Can you give me a framework for solving complex workplace problems?

explain.say: Today we explore three key professional skills. These are teamwork, leadership, and problem-solving. Each skill is vital for career success.
Teamwork means coordinating efforts toward a shared goal. A concrete example is a marketing team planning a product launch. Everyone contributes their specific expertise.
Leadership involves taking initiative and guiding the group process. For example, when a project stalls, a leader steps up to organize a brainstorming session. They keep the focus clear.

Problem-solving is the systematic process of identifying issues and developing viable solutions. Consider analyzing why customer complaints suddenly increased last month. You must investigate the root cause.

In a real workplace scenario, imagine a tight deadline for a major report. Good teamwork divides the sections fairly. Leadership ensures everyone meets their mini-deadlines. Problem-solving helps fix any late sections quickly.
A common mistake is assuming one person must solve everything alone. To avoid this, always use the 'ask' method. Instead of giving answers, ask open-ended questions to guide the group's thinking.

draw.text: Mistake: Solving Alone. Fix: Ask Questions.

faq.q: How do I know if I am a natural leader?
faq.a: Natural leadership often shows up when you are reliable and good at listening to others. You might also find yourself naturally organizing group efforts.

faq.q: Is teamwork just about dividing tasks equally?
faq.a: No, teamwork is about synergy, where the combined output is greater than the sum of individual efforts. It requires mutual support and trust.
asks: Does teamwork mean everyone does the same thing?
What is the core of teamwork?
Is teamwork just dividing the work?

faq.q: When should I use problem-solving skills?
faq.a: You should use them whenever there is a gap between the current state and the desired outcome. This applies in daily tasks or major projects.
asks: Is problem-solving only for big issues?

faq.q: Does leadership mean being the loudest person in the room?
faq.a: Not at all. Effective leadership often means being the calmest and most thoughtful person. It is about influence, not volume.
asks: Must a leader speak the most?
Is quiet confidence a form of leadership?
How is leadership different from talking a lot?

faq.q: How do I balance teamwork with my own ideas?
faq.a: You balance it by presenting your ideas as suggestions that enhance the group's existing work. Frame it as an addition, not a replacement.
asks: Keeping my voice heard in a team?

facts: Effective teamwork requires clear communication channels among all members.
Leadership is often defined by the ability to motivate and guide people toward a vision.
Problem-solving methodologies encourage critical thinking and structured analysis.
Synergy, the core of teamwork, means the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.

quiz.say: A group needs to decide on a new company slogan. The best approach involves:

options.show: Immediately voting on the three best ideas.
options.say: Immediately voting on the three best ideas.

options.show: Asking only the senior managers for suggestions.
options.say: Asking only the senior managers for suggestions.

options.show: Having one person write down all the suggestions.
options.say: Having one person write down all the suggestions.

quiz.why: Generating many diverse ideas first maximizes the pool of options before narrowing down.

wrong.0: This limits creativity by forcing early decisions.
wrong.1: This ignores valuable input from other team members.
wrong.2: This can lead to ideas being lost or misinterpreted.

quiz.say: If a project timeline slips because of unforeseen technical issues, the most crucial skill to deploy is:

options.show: Telling the client the delay is unavoidable.
options.say: Telling the client the delay is unavoidable.

options.show: Asking the team to work longer hours without breaks.
options.say: Asking the team to work longer hours without breaks.

options.show: Analyzing the technical failure to find a workaround.
options.say: Analyzing the technical failure to find a workaround.

options.show: Assigning blame to the department that caused the delay.
options.say: Assigning blame to the department that caused the delay.

quiz.why: Problem-solving requires diagnosing the root cause of the delay to create a recovery plan.

wrong.0: This shows a lack of proactive management and solutions.
wrong.1: Burnout reduces cognitive function, making better solutions unlikely.
wrong.3: Blame-finding stops progress and damages team morale.

quiz.say: A team leader notices two members are arguing over the best strategy. The leader should:

options.show: Facilitate a structured discussion where both sides present evidence.
options.say: Facilitate a structured discussion where both sides present evidence.

options.show: Tell the arguing members to stop immediately.
options.say: Tell the arguing members to stop immediately.

options.show: Decide on a strategy without consulting them.
options.say: Decide on a strategy without consulting them.

options.show: Ignore the argument and move to the next agenda item.
options.say: Ignore the argument and move to the next agenda item.

quiz.why: Facilitating ensures the focus remains on the evidence and the goal, not the conflict.

wrong.1: This suppresses the conflict without resolving the underlying disagreement.
wrong.2: This undermines the team's buy-in and sense of ownership.
wrong.3: Unresolved conflict will resurface later, potentially causing a bigger issue.
